item.title: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.35
How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles Editor's Note American Airlines AAdvantage miles are some of my favorite rewards to earn and redeem. And there are plenty of ways to earn AAdvantage miles, whether you frequently fly American Airlines or earn miles through American Airlines credit cards and other partners. In fact, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is currently offering its highest-ever welcome offer following its August refresh. For a limited time, the card has a welcome offer of 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Whether you're sitting on a large balance already or considering this welcome offer, here's what you should know about redeeming American AAdvantage miles. How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for flights As with most airline miles, the best way to redeem AAdvantage miles is usually for flights. You can easily search and book one-way, round-trip and multicity itineraries operated by American Airlines and most of its partners on the American Airlines website or app. To do so, enter your origin, destination, travel date and number of passengers, plus whether you want to book one-way or round-trip. (If you want to book multicity, click "Advanced / multi-city search.") Then, click the "Redeem miles" box. Results for your search will appear. You can sort these results by award price, duration, arrival time and departure time. You can also filter the results by the number of stops, operating carrier and airport (for destinations with multiple nearby airports). And if you have flexible travel dates, you can click on "Calendar" to see how award rates on your route compare across the entire month. Once you find an award you like, click on its tile. A trip summary showing the itinerary and its cost in miles, and taxes and fees will load. You'll need to log into your AAdvantage account at this point if you haven't already. On the next page, enter or confirm the traveler's details and trip contact information. Click through to the next page to buy a mileage multiplier if you wish. Otherwise, you can select seats on the next page. On the following page, you can buy checked bags. Then, you'll reach the final booking page. You'll need to select whether to buy insurance before you can enter your payment information and ticket your trip. If you are flexible regarding your travel destination, you can use the award map feature. However, based on my experience, it often doesn't show all the lowest-priced award destinations you could book. I recommend using Seats.aero if you want to see broad ways to use AAdvantage miles from a particular origin. You can generally cancel an unused American Airlines AAdvantage award before departure and have your miles reinstated without a fee. You can also change many awards, though your itinerary may be repriced and require additional miles. Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value Redeeming AAdvantage miles for American Airlines flights AAdvantage prices American Airlines award flights dynamically, so there isn't a fixed award chart that defines how many miles these flights cost. Instead, the award cost of these flights can vary drastically based on date, departure time, when you book and more. For example, AAdvantage award flights can vary significantly in mileage cost, even on flights that are just a few hours apart. You can book Main Cabin economy award flights on American Airlines-operated flights, as well as premium economy, business-class and first-class awards, through AAdvantage. Of course, the cabins you can book on any given flight may vary based on what's available on that aircraft type and what American makes available for award bookings. Related: Can you transfer American Airlines AAdvantage miles? Redeeming AAdvantage miles for partner flights AAdvantage has Oneworld partners as well as non-Oneworld partners like Aer Lingus and Etihad Airways that you can book with American Airlines miles. While American-operated AAdvantage awards use dynamic award pricing, most partner awards follow the American Airlines AAdvantage partner award charts. And if even just one leg of your itinerary is operated by a partner, the award pricing will usually follow the partner award charts. For example, here's the AAdvantage partner award chart for one-way itineraries that start in the continental U.S. or Canada: | Destination | Main cabin off-peak | Main cabin | Premium economy | Business/first | First | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Contiguous 48 U.S. states and Canada | N/A | 12,500 miles | 22,500 miles | 25,000 miles | 50,000 miles | | Alaska | N/A | 15,000 miles | 25,000 miles | 30,000 miles | 55,000 miles | | Hawaii | N/A | 22,500 miles | 50,000 miles | 55,000 miles | 80,000 miles | | Caribbean, Mexico or Central America | N/A | 17,500 miles | N/A | 27,500 miles | 52,500 miles | | South America Region 1 | N/A | 20,000 miles | N/A | 30,000 miles | 55,000 miles | | South America Region 2 | N/A | 30,000 miles | 40,000 miles | 57,500 miles | 85,000 miles | | Europe | 22,500 miles | 30,000 miles | 40,000 miles | 57,500 miles | 85,000 miles | | Middle East | N/A | 40,000 miles | 62,500 miles | 70,000 miles | 115,000 miles | | Indian Subcontinent | N/A | 40,000 miles | 62,500 miles | 70,000 miles | 115,000 miles | | Africa | N/A | 40,000 miles | 65,000 miles | 75,000 miles | 120,000 miles | | Asia Region 1 | N/A | 35,000 miles | 50,000 miles | 60,000 miles | 80,000 miles | | Asia Region 2 | N/A | 37,500 miles | 50,000 miles | 70,000 miles | 110,000 miles | | South Pacific | N/A | 40,000 miles | 65,000 miles | 80,000 miles | 110,000 miles | However, there are always exclusions at the bottom of each AAdvantage partner award chart. For this one, business- and first-class awards that include travel on an aircraft with lie-flat seats in the U.S. and Canada cost 7,500 miles more than is shown. Plus, you can only travel in certain directions or transit certain regions when traveling to some regions. And unfortunately, not every partner award follows these rates. Awards operated by Fiji Airways and Air Tahiti Nui use dynamic pricing, so you may see rates significantly higher than those shown on the partner award chart. For example, a nonstop economy Fiji Airways flight might cost 28,000 miles one day and 100,000 miles the next. Additionally, it's worth remembering that the taxes and fees can vary drastically not only by route but also by operating airline. In particular, awards with segments operated by British Airways often have high taxes and fees. Luckily, you'll see the taxes and fees when you search for awards on the American Airlines website or app. Related: Why American Airlines AAdvantage has become my most valuable rewards currency Other ways to redeem AAdvantage miles It's usually best to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for flights, but you do have some other options. Flight upgrades You can redeem miles to upgrade American Airlines and Qantas flights. Head to the American Airlines website or app and find your trip to upgrade American Airlines flights. Once you open your trip, you'll likely see an upgrade offer under your trip details. In this case, I could redeem 63,900 miles or pay $584 for an upgrade on a three-hour flight. Redeeming miles for this upgrade would yield only 0.91 cents per mile, which is significantly less than TPG's September 2026 valuation of AAdvantage miles. For Qantas flights, you can request an upgrade with AAdvantage miles if you booked an eligible trip. You'll find out 24 hours before departure whether your upgrade has cleared. Head to this page to enter your confirmation code and last name to see if your trip is eligible. Seats on American Airlines-operated flights You can also redeem AAdvantage miles for seats on American-operated flights. In this example, you could redeem 7,300 to 8,300 miles or pay $70 to $80 for Main Cabin Extra seats. However, doing so will only give you 0.96 cents per mile, which is significantly lower than TPG's valuation of AAdvantage miles. Admirals Club access You can also redeem American miles for Admirals Club access in the form of a one-day pass or membership. One-day passes cost 7,900 AAdvantage miles or $79, while annual memberships that provide individual access to nearly 50 Admirals Club lounges cost 75,000 miles or $750. Meanwhile, annual memberships that provide access for you and up to two guests to more than 100 Admirals Club lounges and partner lounges worldwide vary as follows based on your AAdvantage elite status tier: - Member: 140,000 miles or $1,400 - Gold: 135,000 miles or $1,350 - Platinum: 130,000 miles or $1,300 - Platinum Pro: 125,000 miles or $1,250 - Executive Platinum: 120,000 miles or $1,200 As you can see, you'll only get 1 cent per mile when redeeming AAdvantage miles for an Admirals Club membership or a one-day pass. For many AAdvantage members, getting the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard — which provides the primary cardholder full membership access privileges to Admirals Club lounges — will be a much better option than redeeming miles for lounge access. Related: 3 reasons why this is the best card for Admirals Club lounge access Five Star Service You can also redeem American miles for Five Star Service at 16 U.S. airports if you have a first- or business-class ticket. Five Star Service provides: - Access to Flagship First check-in (or priority check-in if Flagship First check-in is unavailable) - Admirals Club lounge access - Personalized service through the airport - Priority boarding and reaccommodation - Car service coordination Five Star Service costs 35,000 miles or $350 for the first person, plus 10,000 miles or $100 per additional adult and 5,000 miles or $50 per child 17 and under if there are five or fewer people in your party. Otherwise, you'll need to pay an additional $350 for an additional Five Star Service greeter for every five additional travelers in your party. Related: A complete guide to VIP concierge services to upgrade your airport experience Hotel, rental car, cruise and vacation bookings It's also possible to redeem American miles for hotel bookings through the AAdvantage Hotels platform, rental cars through the AAdvantage Cars platform, cruises through the AAdvantage Cruises platform and vacation packages through the AAdvantage Vacations platform. However, these platforms are usually better used for earning miles and Loyalty Points than for redemptions, as they typically offer only 1 cent per mile or less. Experiences, gift cards and merchandise Finally, you can also redeem American miles for Ticketmaster tickets on the AAdvantage Events platform, merchandise through the AAdvantage Exchange platform and gift cards through the AAdvantage Gift Cards platform. And if you are a Citi / AAdvantage cardholder, you can redeem American miles to book Mastercard Priceless experiences. However, don't expect any of these options to give you outsize value. Even with an AAdvantage cardholder discount, I'd still only get 0.7 cents per mile when redeeming for an Amazon gift card. Related: The 8 best ways to redeem up to 100,000 American Airlines AAdvantage miles How much are American Airlines AAdvantage miles worth? Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, American AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each. This valuation is based on the AAdvantage awards Points Path users saw during searches over a three-month window before the valuations were published. As such, it represents the value you can get from AAdvantage miles if you don't try to maximize them. As a reminder, you can compare your redemption rate — the comparable paid rate minus the taxes and fees you'd pay on the award, all divided by the award's mileage cost — to TPG's valuation to determine whether you're getting decent value on your redemption. American Airlines AAdvantage prices its own flights dynamically, but you may still see some very high or low redemption rates. Meanwhile, partner-operated awards that follow an award chart may offer poor value on some routes but outsize value on others. In particular, you can often get great value when booking long-haul premium cabin awards operated by partner airlines like Qatar Airways and Japan Airlines. Related: How TPG determines its points and miles valuations Bottom line American Airlines AAdvantage miles can be extremely useful, especially since you can redeem them for flights on American and a wide range of partner airlines. American-operated awards use dynamic pricing, while most partner awards still start at published award chart rates. So, having flexible travel dates and comparing your options can help you stretch your miles further. You can also redeem AAdvantage miles for upgrades, seats, Admirals Club access, hotels, rental cars, cruises, vacation packages and more. However, many of these options only give a redemption rate of 1 cent per mile or less. So, I prefer to save my AAdvantage miles for flights, including high-value partner-operated awards. Frequently asked questions American Airlines AAdvantage says its flights start at 7,500 miles each way, although you'll occasionally find less-expensive awards. American uses dynamic pricing for its flights, while most partner awards start at the rates shown on American's partner award charts. You can redeem AAdvantage miles for flights on American's Oneworld partners, as well as non-Oneworld partners such as Aer Lingus and Etihad Airways. Most of these partner awards follow American's partner award charts, although Fiji Airways and Air Tahiti Nui awards use dynamic pricing. You can usually cancel an unused AAdvantage award before departure and have your miles reinstated without a fee. Many awards can also be changed, though the new itinerary may be repriced and require additional miles. TPG values American Airlines AAdvantage miles at 1.45 cents each as of September 2026. Your actual redemption value can vary significantly depending on the award, with some partner premium cabin awards offering significantly more value. You can redeem AAdvantage miles for hotels through AAdvantage Hotels and rental cars through AAdvantage Cars. You can also use miles for cruises and vacation packages, but these redemptions typically offer around 1 cent per mile or less.

item.title: Atmos Summit card: Why it's the most rewarding airline card to maximize international travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.44
Atmos Summit card: Why it's the most rewarding airline card to maximize international travel If the Atmos Rewards loyalty program isn't on your radar yet, it's time to buckle up and pay attention. Born from the merger of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, this program has quietly become one of the most valuable in the industry, with an award chart full of sweet spots. And the premium Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card is the best way to quickly rack up those points, especially if you travel internationally. That's because, in addition to the impressive welcome bonus, the Summit card earns an impressive 3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar spent on foreign purchases. That's not just dining or travel, but every purchase made in a foreign currency. When you're traveling abroad, the last thing you want is to have to figure out which card to use for each transaction. With the Summit card, it's all you need. Here's why this single earning rate makes the card the market leader for international travelers. Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite credit card: Earn 80,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. Related: My take on Alaska's unified Atmos Rewards program Why the Summit's foreign purchases earning rate puts this card in a league of its own At TPG's September 2026 valuation of Atmos Rewards points, earning 3 points per dollar on foreign purchases translates to 4.65 cents of value per dollar spent abroad. Eligible Bank of America account holders can do even better, receiving a 10% rewards bonus on points earned from card purchases. That boosts the return on eligible foreign transactions to 3.3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar, worth about 5.12 cents per dollar at TPG's September 2026 valuation. That's an exceptional return on purchases that would otherwise fall outside other airline cards' bonus categories. The beauty of the Summit card is its simplicity. There are no rotating categories to activate, no cap on bonus earnings and no confusion about merchant codes or time zones. Every eligible foreign transaction earns the same generous rate, whether you're paying for a hotel in Tokyo, a train ticket in Switzerland or groceries in Mexico. TPG contributing editor Matt Moffitt, who recently relocated to Spain, now uses the Summit card for all non-dining purchases. Though the American Express® Gold Card still edges ahead in one single category, dining at 4 points per dollar spent at restaurants worldwide (on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, the 1 point per dollar spent thereafter), Amex acceptance outside the U.S. can be inconsistent, something Matt doesn't face with the Summit's worldwide Visa network. How the Atmos Summit compares with other premium airline cards' international earning rates The Summit card earns: - Unlimited 3 points per dollar spent on eligible worldwide dining, Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases and all foreign transactions - Unlimited 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (such as supermarkets within the United States) The card has an annual fee of $395. Most premium airline cards with similar annual fees offer bonus points or miles in a limited number of select travel categories and 1 point or mile per dollar spent on everything else, but none match the Summit's blanket 3 points per dollar spent on foreign purchases: - The Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings, 3 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases, but only 2 miles per dollar spent on dining and eligible "Rides and Rails", and just 1 mile per dollar spent on other purchases. - The Delta SkyMiles® Platinum American Express Card with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns a similar 3 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases and purchases made directly with hotels, but only 2 miles per dollar spent on restaurants worldwide including takeout and delivery in the U.S., and at U.S. supermarkets, and 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. - The United Quest℠ Card with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns 5 miles per dollar on prepaid hotel stays booked through Renowned Hotels and Resorts, 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible United flights, 4 miles per dollar spent on all other United purchases, 2 miles per dollar spent on dining, select streaming services and other travel, and 1 mile per dollar spent on all other purchases. None of these cards comprehensively reward the routine spending that makes up the bulk of what travelers actually charge abroad: groceries, transportation, shopping and incidental expenses. Meanwhile, the Summit card generously and innovatively rewards you for being an international traveler. Other Atmos Summit benefits The foreign-earnings rate is my favorite feature, but the Summit's broader offering justifies its $395 annual fee for frequent travelers, whether they travel domestically or internationally. The current welcome offer delivers decent value: earn 80,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. The Global Companion Award offers a discount of up to 25,000 points (or 100,000 points after $60,000 or more on purchases each anniversary year) on the second passenger's ticket when you book two people traveling together with Atmos Rewards points. Uniquely, it is valid for travel on Alaska Airlines and all of its airline redemption partners, both in and outside of the Oneworld alliance, in any cabin — including Hawaiian Airlines, British Airways, Qantas, Iberia, Icelandair, Korean Air and others. Applicable fees and taxes still apply. The card also offers a host of other travel benefits, including anniversary status points, a pathway to elite status, lounge and Wi-Fi passes, waived same-day confirmed flight change fee and free checked baggage on Alaska and Hawaiian flights. You don't need to fly Alaska to get amazing value from Atmos Rewards points Even if you've never flown Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines, Atmos Rewards points can deliver amazing value through partner redemptions. The program inherited Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan's award chart, which has long been a favorite among points and miles enthusiasts for its outsize value on partner airlines. The sweet spots span virtually every region of the globe. You can book an American Airlines flight of up to 700 miles in length for just 4,500 Atmos Rewards points, or fly Hawaiian Airlines economy from the West Coast to Hawaii from 10,000 points. Looking to cross the Atlantic? Aer Lingus business class to Ireland starts at just 45,000 points. For aspirational redemptions, 75,000 points can get you a seat on Japan Airlines' business class from the West Coast to Tokyo, or Fiji Airways business class to Fiji. Bottom line Earning 3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar spent on every eligible transaction abroad — worth 4.65 cents per dollar at TPG's September 2026 valuations — is unmatched by any other airline card. If you haven't been paying attention to Atmos Rewards, consider this your wake-up call. With broad earning abroad, useful travel perks and a valuable partner redemption chart, the Atmos Rewards Summit card is an incredible companion to pack with your passport. And right now, the card is offering a great welcome offer: Earn 80,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. If international travel is part of your life, this card should be, too.
